modules.title: Parallel-beam Radon projection and filtered backprojection
modules.expensive_path: For each projection angle, radon rotates and interpolates an image and sums the rays; iradon filters the sinogram with FFTs and interpolates each filtered projection onto every reconstruction pixel. The image-by-angle loops grow with image area and projection count, and independent slices provide an additional batch dimension. Native timings are reported separately; no GPU speedup is claimed.
modules.rationale: The forward projector and its analytical inverse form one independently useful parallel-beam tomography workflow with explicit image coordinates and an established upstream phantom example. The source path is a containing file: only the four named symbols are in this first module. Its other two symbols implement the separately deferred iterative SART workflow.
excluded: iradon_sart and order_angles_golden_ratio in the same containing file: iterative ray updates and ordering form a separate numerical method and are outside the previously selected first-task scope.
src/skimage/transform/finite_radon_transform.py: a finite integer transform on prime-sized arrays, with a different mathematical and output contract.
General geometric transformations and interpolation APIs: dependencies are retained in the source payload, but only their execution within radon and iradon is in the proposed task.
All other image-processing subpackages: retained as upstream source but not proposed as additional tasks in this contribution.
hazards: Even/odd dimensions, centre conventions, cropping, padding and the reconstruction-circle mask affect the physical pixel coordinates.
Float32 versus float64, interpolation choices and FFT summation order can change values; later task tolerances need measured evidence and human finalisation.
The upstream random-circle fixture resets NumPy's RNG. Task inputs must be frozen by the reference-side fixture preparation, not generated by a candidate sampler.
The upstream circle reconstruction helper calls np.allclose without asserting it; a passing native test is not evidence that this particular comparison held.
The upstream test_iradon_angles assigns nb_angles=80 but reuses the previously generated 200-angle theta array; it does not test the advertised reduced-angle case.
The _radon_transform Cython extension is imported by the containing module for the deferred SART entry point. It must still build for the unmodified reference package.
Only the Radon test file and tomography example are investigated natively; the entire library's test suite is inventoried but is not claimed to pass.

The source path is a containing file: only the four named symbols are in this first module. Its other two symbols implement the separately deferred iterative SART workflow.
primary_inputs: A two-dimensional image or parallel-beam sinogram with explicitly ordered image coordinates.
Projection angles, output size, circle and range options, Fourier filter and interpolation selection.
primary_outputs: A two-dimensional sinogram indexed by detector coordinate and projection angle.
A reconstructed two-dimensional image indexed by the original spatial pixel coordinates.
algorithm_stages: Convert image range and dtype; crop to an inscribed circle or pad while preserving the rotation centre.
Rotate/interpolate the image for each angle and integrate detector rays.
Pad projections, form the selected Fourier filter, and filter with FFT/IFFT.
Interpolate each filtered projection onto the output grid; accumulate, normalize and apply the circle mask.

modules.differences: This is the analytical projector/FBP workflow. SART uses iterative image corrections and angle ordering; the finite Radon transform has an integer/prime-grid contract. Neither is part of the selected first task. File-level accounting includes the full 536-line containing file; the four selected functions span 302 physical lines.
